subtitle: A status report from UCSB and RAND sites on their network implementation

tldr.problem: UCSB and RAND needed to verify that their newly developed Network Control Programs were operating correctly according to the protocol specification.
tldr.mechanism: The two sites conducted direct console-to-console testing between their NCPs, exercising basic protocol exchanges to confirm correct behavior according to Document #1.
tldr.outcome: Both NCPs worked as specified. RAND found minor issues in their Network Services Program interface, mostly related to data format conversion and display concerns, not protocol problems.

today: RFC 78 is a historical status report and has not been obsoleted. It provides early evidence of ARPANET implementations working correctly.

sections.title: NCP Checkout Results
sections.content:
RFC 78 reports on validation testing conducted jointly by UCSB and RAND on their Network Control Program implementations. The exercise involved console-to-console testing to verify that both NCPs behaved according to the protocol specification in Document #1.

The RFC was authored by E. Harslem, J. Heafner, and J. White from UCSB and RAND respectively, providing an early account of intersite protocol verification on the ARPANET.
sections.plainLanguage: Two network teams tested their programs by sending messages back and forth through their network boxes.

sections.title: Testing Outcomes and Minor Issues
sections.content:
Both UCSB and RAND NCPs responded correctly to the testing and behaved as specified in Document #1. RAND discovered a few minor problems, but these were not in the NCP itself. Instead, the issues appeared in the Network Services Program (NSP), which bridges the gap between the NCP and video graphics consoles.

The problems were limited to data format conversions and human factors aspects of displaying status information. No fundamental protocol problems were discovered.
sections.plainLanguage: The core programs worked fine. The only problems were in how the computer showed what was happening on the screen.

sections.title: Next Steps
sections.content:
Both sites expressed willingness to participate in further NCP validation exercises with other ARPANET sites. They planned additional testing involving data reconfigurations and file transmissions to expand their understanding of protocol behavior under different conditions.

This report exemplifies the collaborative, pragmatic approach taken by early ARPANET implementers as they worked to ensure protocol correctness across different sites.
sections.plainLanguage: The teams said they would be happy to test with other sites and try more complicated message flows.
